abstract: Protein language models (pLMs) typically tokenize sequences at the single-amino-acid level using a 20-residue alphabet, resulting in long input sequences and high computational cost. Sub-word tokenization methods such as Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) can reduce sequence length but are limited by the sparsity of long patterns in proteins encoded by the standard amino acid alphabet. Reduced amino acid alphabets, which group residues by physicochemical properties, offer a potential solution but their performances with sub-word tokenization have not been systematically studied. In this work, we investigate the combined use of reduced amino acid alphabets and BPE tokenization in protein language models. We pre-train RoBERTa-based pLMs de novo using multiple reduced alphabets and evaluate them across diverse downstream tasks. Our results show that reduced alphabets enable substantially shorter input sequences and faster training and inference. These findings suggest that alphabet reduction may facilitate more effective sub-word tokenization, enabling increased efficiency with marginal impact on predictive performance, and for specific tasks even improving accuracy.
